ai.seo_question: What is the religious status of using perfume in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Al-Abbas ibn Musa narrates from his father that perfume is a Sunnah of the Prophets, a concise statement that elevates personal grooming to a spiritual tradition. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the permissibility and recommendation of using scent, linking physical cleanliness to prophetic emulation. It reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on beauty and hygiene as acts of worship when done with the right intention.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Abbas son of Musa<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘
I heard my fatherasws saying: ‘The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ’Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-‘Abbas ibn Musa who has said the following:
I heard my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Al-‘Atr (perfume) is of the Sunnah of the messengers (of Allah).”’
